title: Lesson Plan — Development (Class 10 CBSE Economics)
subject: Social Science (Economics)
objectives: Explain why people have different development goals.
Use per capita income to compare countries and recall World Bank classifications.
Identify three limitations of income as a measure of development.
Describe the role of public facilities in development.
Use IMR, literacy, life expectancy and net attendance to compare Indian states.
Explain the Human Development Index and discuss sustainability.
prerequisites: Knowledge of basic terms — income, expenditure, government, public services.
Comfort reading a small data table.
materials: Printed Indian state data table (Kerala / Haryana / Bihar) on PCI, IMR, literacy
A short story / image of a rural well drying up

activities.description: Hook: 'What is development?' Take quick answers from 5 students of different backgrounds (or imagined ones — farmer, banker, mother, factory worker, adivasi). Note the variety on the board.
Hand out a small table of three states (Kerala / Haryana / Bihar) with PCI, IMR, literacy. In pairs, students rank the states on income; then on IMR; then on literacy. Discuss why ranks differ.

Cover four blocks: (i) different people, different goals + national-development question; (ii) per capita income + World Bank groups + limitations; (iii) public facilities + non-income indicators; (iv) HDI + sustainability.
teacher_actions: Define per capita income on the board.
List the four indicators (IMR / literacy / NAR / life expectancy).
student_actions: Compute one PCI on the board.
List two examples of public facilities.

activities.description: Worksheet practice: 6 questions covering definitions, the three-state comparison, HDI, and a short reading on a sustainability dilemma.
Exit ticket: 4 questions, one from each block.
Homework: ask 3 family members what 'development' means for them; record their answers; classify each as material or non-material.
teacher_actions: Bridge to next chapter (Sectors of the Indian Economy).

homework: Ask 3 family members what 'development' means for them; classify each answer as material / non-material.
Find your state's IMR and literacy rate and compare them with Kerala and Bihar.
Write a short paragraph: 'Is groundwater being used sustainably in my region?'
assessment_ideas: Use the 4-item exit ticket as formative.
Run a 10-question quiz next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on public facilities with a 5-point rubric.
references: NCERT Class 10 — Understanding Economic Development, Chapter 1: Development.
